summary: A test-the-claim series. The hook (0 to about 7 s) puts the claim being tested in a rounded inset on the left: another creator's clip with its own captions, or a repo page with a picture-in-picture. The speaker stands to its right, and a white 'Fact or Hype?' pill sits above his head. A cut to a wider shot of the speaker then lands 'IS IT FACT OR HYPE' as huge yellow italic words with a black outline on the chest, for about 1.5-2 s. From then to the end, a checkbox bar reading FACT / OR / HYPE (with an emoji) sits across the chest at y≈50-52 %, and a teal-framed panel fills the lower half with a screen recording of him running the test. The panel changes content every few seconds, and those changes produce most of the cut detections. The speaker is filmed medium, unscripted, at a desk; his own voice is not captioned, and the voice is cut tight (≤2.7 pauses/min). His own text is limited to three treatments, so the format is carried by layout and structure, not by text density.

hook.what: State the claim over its source, under the series pill.

body.what: Ask the question (stack), then run the test live in the panel under the open checkboxes; say aloud what would make it a fact (shown typed in the app in 2 of 3 reels, e.g. 'If this works, then it's a fact').

end.what: The verdict on the bar. The last sampled frames show the result in the panel; the tick itself is not visible.

fit_notes: There are no captions on the speaker's own voice. For a Thai or sound-off audience, the fit-checker decides whether to add captions.style 'mini' in the gap between the chin and the bar (y ≈ 900-950) or to keep the reel uncaptioned; record which.

The format only makes sense for a clip in which the speaker tests something. Without the test material, the panel and the verdict are dropped, and only the pill and stack remain: say so instead of faking it.
